title: Partner Technical Kickstart - Battlecard Draft
content:
Purpose:
A compact, technical-focused battlecard and kickstart checklist for partner engineering teams and platform partners. Designed for quick pre-call prep, a 20–30 minute demo, and a follow-up validation run the partner can do in their environment.

TL;DR (elevator):
- Redwood Inference = predictable inference performance + routing and clear cost controls across hosted / dedicated / private deployments.
- Quick win to demo: latency-stable text generation for product search assist, and an embeddings-based semantic search proof-of-concept with <1s median latency for small queries.

Target persona(s):
- Platform/Infra engineering lead (wants isolation + SLA)
- ML engineer (wants model quality + inference cost controls)
- Solutions/Integration engineer (needs reproducible steps to onboard)

Call agenda (20–30min):
1) 3 min: quick intro + success criteria (what does a win look like for them?)
2) 7 min: architecture + differentiation (routing, batching, quantization options)
3) 8 min: live demo (hosted API: generation + embeddings, show cost/latency dashboard)
4) 5 min: validation plan + next steps (pilot, dedicated sizing, private kickoff)

Pre-call prep checklist (sales/SE):
- Confirm which environment they care about (hosted | dedicated | private).
- Ask for typical payload size, sequence length, qps, and sensitive data constraints.
- Share the short PoC recipe (below) and a dummy API key for a test account if available.

Discovery prompts (quick, open):
- What SLOs are you targeting for tail latency and p50/p95?
- How many concurrent users / requests at peak? What percentile of requests are short (<=64 tokens)?
- How do you measure model quality today? Do you have existing prompt/eval sets?
- Any regulatory or data residency constraints?

Quick tech validation (partner can run these in <20 minutes):
- 1) Simple generation smoke test (hosted):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <TEST_KEY>" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-llm-xt-1","input":"Summarize the following product description in one sentence: "<sample>"","max_tokens":40}'
  Expected: 200–800ms median for short prompts; check request_id and tokens_consumed in response.

- 2) Embedding quickcheck (semantic search):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <TEST_KEY>" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"embed-lite-v1","input":["How do I reset my password?","Change password instructions"]}'
  Expected: vector length ~1536 (model dependent); verify roundtrip and cosine similarity > 0.7 for paraphrases.

- 3) Cost/latency dashboard walkthrough (show the Console):
  - Navigate to Console -> Routes -> Recent requests. Point out token-level cost breakdown and p50/p95 latency.

Competitive talking points (concise):
- Versus cloud-hosted endpoints: Redwood offers unified runtime across hosted, dedicated and private — same API, consistent rollouts and predictable unit economics.
- Versus self-hosted open-source stacks: we provide production hardening: routing, autoscale, KV caching, and SLO-backed capacity for dedicated customers.
- Versus other LLM APIs: transparent cost controls + observability (token and route-level).

Pricing shorthand for convo:
- Hosted: pay-as-you-go (token/embedding units). Good for fast validation and early integration.
- Dedicated: monthly committed capacity; call out predictable unit economics and burst options.
- Private: platform licensing + optional on-prem runtime; emphasize security & compliance integrations (KMS/HSM, audit logs).

Objection handling (short scripts):
- "We need lower cost": propose batching + KV prefix caching + quantized model recommendation via Redwood Optimize. Offer a quick cost-savings estimate during follow-up.
- "We need on-prem for compliance": outline Private offering, show audit log screenshots and KMS integrations; suggest next step = architecture scoping call with SRE.
- "How do we avoid regressions": highlight evals tied to prompt sets, rollouts/canaries, and automatic fallback to older model variants.

Mini demo slide deck outline (5 slides):
1) Problem + customer example (pain + scale)
2) What Redwood does (serving runtime + routing + observability)
3) Live demo screenshots & Console highlights
4) Pilot plan + success metrics (latency, cost per 1M tokens, accuracy delta)
5) Next steps + roles + timeline

Follow-up assets to send after call (email template snippets):
- 1) Quick recap + PoC recipe (attach the simple curl steps above)
- 2) Proposed pilot options: 2-week hosted trial vs 8–12 week dedicated sizing engagement. Include estimated costs (placeholder ranges).

Success metrics we propose to track in pilot:
- p50/p95 latency for typical prompts (target: p50 < 300ms for short prompts when hosted)
- tokens per second / cost per 1M tokens (baseline + after batching)
- quality: evaluation score on partner’s holdout prompt set (show pass/fail criteria)

Internal SE notes / negotiation levers:
- For strategic partners we can offer extended pilot credits and a reduced ramp for first committed quarter. Flag for GTM-sdr to request for exec approval.
- If partner needs private-only, prep SRE scoping template and bring in security lead early.

Open questions to resolve before pilot:
- Do they want GPU affinity for certain model families? (affects Dedicated sizing)
- Expected token distribution (short vs long) — ask for sample logs or a small dataset.
- Data residency / encryption-at-rest expectations for Private.

Next steps checklist (assignable):
- [ ] Send PoC recipe + test key (owner: AE)
- [ ] Schedule 30 min scoping call w/ partner infra + Redwood SRE (owner: SE)
- [ ] Share pilot pricing options (owner: Sales Ops)
- [ ] Add partner to internal pilot tracker (linked JIRA: GO-1289)

Notes-to-self style fragments (raw, leave in doc):
- If they are using vector DB X, call out integration notes (export vectors -> Redwood embeddings for similarity scoring).
- For very latency-sensitive edge cases, mention Dedicated w/ local region routing + burst cache.
- Keep an eye on model quantization tradeoffs for recall-sensitive tasks; arrange a quick bench-run with Research if asked.

Revision history / authorship:
- Drafted 2026-02-14 by Nora Patel. Iteration 1 incorporated SE feedback 2026-03-10 (Ethan + Maya).

End of doc.
